'''''Erica umbellata''''' is a species of plant in the heather family (''[[Ericaceae]]'') native to the western [[Iberian Peninsula]] and northwestern [[Maghreb]].<ref name="CoL" />

==Description==
[[File:23.4.14 Briteiros 117 (14009021322).jpg|thumb|left|''Erica umbellata'' on [[Citânia de Briteiros]]]]
''Erica umbellata'' is a {{convert|10|to|50|cm|abbr=on}} bush. It has young stems with barely marked ribs and reddish-brown bark. It has terminal inflorescences, umbelliform, with 3-6 flowers, without involvement of basal bracteoles. Seeds are ellipsoidal and {{convert|0.5|-|0.6|mm|abbr=on}} long. The [[Corolla (botany)|corolla]] is {{convert|3.5|-|5.5|mm|abbr=on}} intensely pink or purple, occasionally albino.<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=Erica umbellata |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/04_074_01_Erica.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=2 March 2021}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
[[File:Erica umbellata Habitus 2009May10 SierraMadrona.jpg|thumb|left|''Erica umbellata'' on a siliceous soil]]
''Erica umbellata'' is native to the western [[Iberian Peninsula]] ([[Portugal]] and western [[Spain]]) and northwest Africa in [[Morocco]]. Inhabiting bare terrain, dwarf or cleared heaths, scrublands, cleared forests, pine forests and subcoastal sand, always on siliceous soils, from sea-level to {{convert|1500|m|abbr=on}} altitude. Some populations in the [[Algarve]] have very large flowers (up to {{convert|7|mm|abbr=on}}) and were denominated var. ''major''. [[Galicia (Spain)|Galician]] plants with graceful stems and small flowers were described as var. ''filiformis''. Rarely some plants appear with rudimentary or aborted stamens (var. ''Anandra'').<ref name="iberica" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Erica umbellata L |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/1Erica+umbellata |publisher=[[Flora-On]] |access-date=2 March 2021}}</ref> ''E. umbellata'' can grow well on [[Agricultural lime|limey]] soils.<ref name=Proudley>{{cite book |author1=Brian Proudley |author2=Valerie Proudley |title=Heathers in Colour |date=1989 |publisher=Blandford Press |isbn=0713714204 |page=38 |edition=2nd |quote=Other fairly lime-tolerant species are ''E. umbellata'' and ''E. terminalis'', both of value for colour in early summer.}}</ref>
